l4_steps.name: Monitor flight status vs published schedule
l4_steps.input: Real-time gate departure feeds, OPS messages, ACARS pushback events
l4_steps.output: Live flight status dashboard with variance-from-schedule flag
l4_steps.kpi: On-time departure (D0) ≥78%; delay detection latency <2 min of STD
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS position reports lag by 90–120 sec on older aircraft, masking initial delay onset until gate hold is already confirmed

l4_steps.name: Apply IATA delay threshold trigger rule
l4_steps.input: Actual vs scheduled departure time delta from AMS feed
l4_steps.output: Delay event record opened in Altéa OC with severity tier (Minor <15 min / Moderate 15–60 min / Severe >60 min)
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of delays ≥15 min captured within 3 min of threshold breach
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa OC severity tiers are configurable per airline but default thresholds may not align with local slot-loss rules at congested airports such as LHR or JFK

l4_steps.name: Assign IATA AHM 730 delay code to event
l4_steps.input: Initial cause report from handling agent, crew, or ATC
l4_steps.output: Primary IATA two-digit delay code + sub-code entered in Altéa OC event record
l4_steps.kpi: Delay code accuracy rate ≥94% (validated at post-ops audit); code entry within 10 min of ETD revision
l4_steps.pain_point: Controllers under workload pressure default to code 93 (unknown) or airline-internal codes; post-ops correction consumes analyst time and distorts monthly reporting

l4_steps.name: Map downstream flight propagation impact
l4_steps.input: Delay event record from Altéa OC; rotational aircraft tail number; planned schedule SSIM
l4_steps.output: Propagation impact list — all subsequent flights on same tail affected with estimated knock-on delay per flight
l4_steps.kpi: Propagation analysis completed within 5 min of delay event creation; ≥95% of knock-on delays correctly identified
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyWORKS propagation engine requires manual tail-number linkage for ad-hoc swaps executed earlier in the day; stale tail assignments cause phantom impact estimates

l4_steps.name: Check crew duty time legality under FAR Part 117
l4_steps.input: Crew pairing records, revised ETD/ETA, accumulated flight duty period (FDP) totals
l4_steps.output: Crew legality status per affected flight: Legal / At-limit / Illegal flag with exact remaining FDP minutes
l4_steps.kpi: Zero FAR Part 117 exceedances; crew illegality flag generated within 3 min of delay event propagation
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen CMS and Altéa OC use separate crew-to-flight linkage tables; sync latency of up to 8 min means early illegality flags can appear after the aircraft has already pushed

l4_steps.name: Identify passenger misconnection risk
l4_steps.input: Passenger booking itineraries with MCT data; revised inbound ETA; connecting flight boarding-complete times
l4_steps.output: At-risk passenger list with booking reference, connection flight, and protection options (next available / hotel voucher eligible)
l4_steps.kpi: Misconnect identification completed before inbound landing (≥30 min ahead); protected reaccommodation rate ≥88% same-day
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa DCS minimum connect time (MCT) tables require manual update when airports revise terminal layouts; outdated MCTs cause under- or over-protection triggering either rebooking churn or missed misconnects

l4_steps.name: Assess whether delay qualifies for EC 261 compensation
l4_steps.input: Delay magnitude; origin/destination country pair; delay cause classification (extraordinary vs controllable)
l4_steps.output: EC 261 / DOT eligibility flag per affected booking; duty-of-care obligations triggered (meal voucher, hotel, rebooking rights)
l4_steps.kpi: EC 261 eligibility flag applied within 5 min of 3-hour delay threshold; 100% of entitled passengers notified before next boarding call
l4_steps.pain_point: Extraordinary-circumstances exemption (weather, ATC) requires documented evidence within 72 hours; NOC controllers rarely capture contemporaneous ATC restriction references, leading to claims upheld in arbitration

l4_steps.name: Generate recovery options — swap, absorb, or cancel
l4_steps.input: Propagation impact list; available spare aircraft inventory; crew availability matrix from Jeppesen CMS
l4_steps.output: Ranked recovery scenario list with estimated schedule recovery time (SRT) and cost-of-delay score per option
l4_steps.kpi: ≥3 ranked scenarios generated within 10 min of escalation trigger; SRT ≤45 min for Moderate tier delays
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyWORKS recovery workspace does not natively score scenarios by total cost-of-delay; controllers rely on manual mental arithmetic, leading to suboptimal aircraft swaps that increase crew costs

l4_steps.name: Evaluate aircraft swap feasibility in SkyMAX
l4_steps.input: Candidate spare aircraft; required range and seat configuration; next-maintenance-due date from AMOS
l4_steps.output: Feasibility verdict: Swap approved / blocked (maintenance hold, wrong config, insufficient range) with reason code
l4_steps.kpi: Aircraft swap evaluation completed within 8 min; maintenance-hold conflicts identified before physical repositioning begins
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyMAX queries AMOS maintenance status via batch API with up to 15-min lag; a maintenance task opened in AMOS after the last sync can result in an illegal swap being physically initiated at the gate

l4_steps.name: Coordinate revised gate and slot with airport ops
l4_steps.system: SITA Airport Management System (AMS) + IATA SLOT coordination message (SSR/SIR)
l4_steps.input: Revised ETD; new aircraft tail; gate resource availability from AMS; slot window from airport coordinator
l4_steps.output: Confirmed gate assignment and revised slot time acknowledged by airport; updated in Altéa OC
l4_steps.kpi: Gate confirmation received ≥30 min before revised ETD; slot revision accepted at slot-controlled airports within IATA SSIM Chapter 8 tolerance window
l4_steps.pain_point: At slot-coordinated airports (Level 3), missing the 15-min retiming window forfeits the slot and forces a new slot request; Altéa OC does not automatically alert the controller when the retiming window is about to expire

l4_steps.name: Approve and lock recovery plan
l4_steps.input: Ranked recovery scenarios; crew legality confirmation from Jeppesen CMS; gate confirmation from AMS
l4_steps.output: Approved recovery plan locked in Altéa OC; task assignments dispatched to ground handling, crew, and ramp teams
l4_steps.kpi: Recovery plan approved and communicated ≥25 min before revised ETD; 0% plan revisions after lock (lock discipline metric)
l4_steps.pain_point: NOC duty managers sometimes approve a plan before crew confirmations are fully resolved, requiring a second re-plan cycle that extends the delay by an additional 20–35 min

l4_steps.name: Broadcast revised ETD to all operational stakeholders
l4_steps.system: SITA ACARS + Telex; Amadeus Altéa OC automated notification
l4_steps.input: Approved recovery plan with locked revised ETD; stakeholder distribution list (crew, ramp, catering, fuelling, ATC)
l4_steps.output: ACARS ETD revision uplink to cockpit; AMS gate board update; SMS/email alerts to ground handlers
l4_steps.kpi: ETD update reaches all stakeholders within 2 min of plan lock; 100% of downstream flights updated in Altéa OC within 5 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Catering and fuelling vendors receive notifications via separate legacy email/fax channels, not through AMS or Altéa; revision propagation to these vendors averages 12 min, risking late catering delivery that re-extends the delay

l4_steps.name: Monitor recovery execution against revised milestones
l4_steps.input: Recovery plan milestones (boarding-complete, doors-close, pushback); real-time gate event feeds
l4_steps.output: Milestone adherence scorecard updated in real time; red flag alert if any milestone slips by >5 min
l4_steps.kpi: Pushback within 3 min of revised ETD for ≥80% of recovery flights; milestone slip detection latency <90 sec
l4_steps.pain_point: AMS milestone tracking relies on manual scan events at gates with intermittent handheld scanner connectivity; at remote stands, missing scan events create false 'on-track' status until ACARS pushback message arrives

l4_steps.name: Close recovery loop and update schedule actuals
l4_steps.input: ACARS airborne message (ATD); gate actual out/off events; confirmed delay duration
l4_steps.output: Delay event record closed in Altéa OC with actual block times; downstream schedule actuals updated; SSIM actual file entry created
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of closed delay events have IATA delay code confirmed within 30 min of ATD; actual block time accuracy ±1 min vs ACARS
l4_steps.pain_point: Controllers frequently forget to close delay events after pushback under high workload; open events accumulate in Altéa OC, inflating active-delay counts and distorting NOC dashboard metrics

l4_steps.name: Aggregate delay evidence and system event logs
l4_steps.system: AWS S3 / Amazon Redshift (Operations Data Lake)
l4_steps.input: Altéa OC event records; AMS gate logs; ACARS messages; Jeppesen crew duty records; weather METAR/SIGMET archive
l4_steps.output: Consolidated delay evidence package in Redshift: one row per delay event with all contributing data sources joined
l4_steps.kpi: Evidence package assembled within 24 hours of flight ops; data completeness ≥97% (all events have linked ACARS record)
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS message archive retention policy varies by data source; some third-party handling agents purge logs after 72 hours, making post-hoc evidence reconstruction impossible for disputes filed after that window

l4_steps.name: Attribute delay causes per IATA AHM 780 methodology
l4_steps.system: Tableau (connected to Redshift delay evidence layer)
l4_steps.input: Consolidated evidence package; IATA AHM 780 attribution rules; airline-defined delay ownership matrix
l4_steps.output: Final delay attribution record: primary cause code, contributing cause codes, responsible department/vendor, accountable cost estimate
l4_steps.kpi: Attribution accuracy ≥94% (audited quarterly by Quality); attribution completed within 48 hours of event for all Severe-tier delays
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA AHM 780 assigns single-cause attribution, but most airline delays are multi-causal; forcing a single code obscures systemic issues (e.g. late catering masked as ATC when both contributed) and skews corrective action priorities

l4_steps.name: Detect systemic delay patterns across rolling 30-day window
l4_steps.input: 30-day delay attribution dataset from Redshift; threshold rules (≥3 events same root cause = systemic flag)
l4_steps.output: Systemic pattern alert: cause code, frequency, affected routes/aircraft type, responsible team, trend direction
l4_steps.kpi: Systemic patterns identified within 5 business days of 3rd occurrence; false-positive pattern rate <10%
l4_steps.pain_point: Pattern detection thresholds are set manually and rarely reviewed; low thresholds generate alert fatigue (managers ignore flags), while high thresholds allow systemic issues to accumulate for 6–8 weeks before escalation

l4_steps.name: Publish delay performance report to operations leadership
l4_steps.input: Final attribution records; systemic pattern alerts; benchmarks (OAG industry OTP data; IATA Annual Review)
l4_steps.output: Weekly delay report: OTP vs target, top-5 delay codes, cost-of-delay by category, systemic patterns open/closed, trend vs prior 4 weeks
l4_steps.kpi: Report published by 08:00 Monday; OTP data currency within 12 hours of end of reporting week
l4_steps.pain_point: Delay cost estimates in the report use average cost-per-minute assumptions (typically €80–100/min CODA benchmark) rather than actual cost data; finance does not integrate actual incremental cost from SAP FI in time for the weekly cycle

l4_steps.name: Submit delay cost attribution to Finance for accrual
l4_steps.system: SAP S/4HANA Finance (FI-CO) — Cost Centre Accounting
l4_steps.input: Final delay attribution records with responsible department; estimated cost-of-delay by category (crew, ground handling, passenger compensation, fuel burn)
l4_steps.output: Cost centre journal entries in SAP FI; EC 261 compensation accrual posted; month-end delay cost reconciliation file
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of Severe-tier delay costs accrued in SAP FI within 5 business days of event; variance between estimated and actual delay cost <15%
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP FI cost centre structure does not granularly distinguish catering vendor delays from ground handler delays; both post to generic 'Ground Services' cost centre, preventing targeted vendor SLA penalty enforcement
